subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Biologists estimate that thousands of bird species engage in seasonal migration worldwide.
• The Arctic tern is one of many birds whose migration route has shifted in recent decades.
• Arctic terns once migrated primarily along western coastlines of the Americas.
• These birds now increasingly follow eastern coastal routes during their journeys.
prompt: The student wants to make and support a generalization about bird migration routes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish these goals?

choices.A: Biologists estimate that thousands of bird species engage in seasonal migration worldwide; some birds' migration routes may shift over time.
choices.B: A bird's migration route may shift over time: the Arctic tern once migrated primarily along western coastlines of the Americas but now increasingly follows eastern coastal routes.
choices.C: Like other animals that travel long distances, thousands of bird species migrate along coastlines around the world.
choices.D: One example of a migratory bird is the Arctic tern, whose migration route once followed primarily western coastlines of the Americas but now increasingly follows eastern coastal routes.

explanation: Choice B is correct. It generalizes that migration routes shift over time, citing Arctic terns that once followed western Americas coastlines but now increasingly use eastern routes.
